units.text: INT. SEAGULL - CONTINUOUS
To TRIGORIN.

When the long autumn evenings descend on us we while away the time here by playing lotto. Look at this old set; we used it when our mother played with us as children. Don’t you want to take a hand in the game with us until supper time?
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: She and TRIGORIN sit down at the table.
It is a monotonous game, but it is all right when one gets used to it.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: She deals three cards to each of the players.
Looking through the pages of the magazine.
He has read his own story, and hasn’t even cut the pages of mine.
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: He lays the magazine on his desk and goes toward the door on the right, stopping as he passes his mother to give her a kiss.
Won’t you play, Constantine?
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: No, excuse me please, I don’t feel like it. I am going to take a turn through the rooms.
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: He goes out.
Are you all ready? I shall begin: twenty-two.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: Here it is.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: Three.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: Right.
units.name: DORN

units.text: Have you put down three? Eight. Eighty-one. Ten.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: Don’t go so fast.
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: Could you believe it? I am still dazed by the reception they gave me in Kharkoff.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: Thirty-four.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: The notes of a melancholy waltz are heard.
The students gave me an ovation; they sent me three baskets of flowers, a wreath, and this thing here.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: She unclasps a brooch from her breast and lays it on the table.
There is something worth while!
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: Fifty.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: Fifty, did you say?
units.name: DORN

units.text: I wore a perfectly magnificent dress; I am no fool when it comes to clothes.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: Constantine is playing again; the poor boy is sad.
units.name: PAULINA

units.text: He has been severely criticised in the papers.
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: Seventy-seven.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: They want to attract attention to him.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: He doesn’t seem able to make a success, he can’t somehow strike the right note. There is an odd vagueness about his writings that sometimes verges on delirium. He has never created a single living character.
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: Eleven.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: Are you bored, Peter?
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: A pause.
He is asleep.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: The Councillor is taking a nap.
units.name: DORN

units.text: Seven. Ninety.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: Do you think I should write if I lived in such a place as this, on the shore of this lake? Never! I should overcome my passion, and give my life up to the catching of fish.
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: Twenty-eight.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: And if I caught a perch or a bass, what bliss it would be!
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: I have great faith in Constantine. I know there is something in him. He thinks in images; his stories are vivid and full of colour, and always affect me deeply. It is only a pity that he has no definite object in view. He creates impressions, and nothing more, and one cannot go far on impressions alone. Are you glad, madam, that you have an author for a son?
units.name: DORN

units.text: Just think, I have never read anything of his; I never have time.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: Twenty-six.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: TREPLIEFF comes in quietly and sits down at his table.
To TRIGORIN.
